items.question: How do service firms in Singapore get clients beyond referrals?
items.answer: Open on a specific need instead of a list of services. A Singapore outsourced CFO firm contacted founders and finance leaders about needs such as monthly management reports or senior finance support, then qualified on their current setup. The campaign booked 19 meetings, led to 6 needs assessments and 3 proposal requests.

items.question: Can an Indian pharma company find licensing partners in Singapore?
items.answer: Yes. An Indian specialty pharma developer reached business development and licensing leaders at Singapore-based pharma businesses and regional teams with an approved, non-confidential product summary. It led to 10 licensing meetings and 4 confidential portfolio reviews. Confidentiality agreements and commercial terms stayed with the client once discussions progressed.

items.question: What rules apply to cold email in Singapore?
items.answer: Singapore's Personal Data Protection Act governs how personal data is collected and used, and the Spam Control Act covers unsolicited commercial email sent in bulk. We keep volumes low, contact business decision-makers only and honour every opt-out. This is general information, not legal advice, so confirm specifics with counsel before scaling.

items.question: How soon will a Singapore campaign book meetings?
items.answer: Campaigns usually go live about 18 days after onboarding, and first qualified conversations typically come in weeks 3 to 4. Singapore is 2.5 hours ahead of India, so messages go out on Singapore weekday mornings and meetings fit an Indian working day. Our four Singapore campaigns booked between 10 and 19 meetings each.
